channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: No agreement on extending Russian sanctions as EU deadline approaches
item.description: European Union member states have still not reached agreement on renewing sanctions against around 3,000 Russian individuals and organisations.

item.title: One injured after reported attack with 'bladed weapon' in Brussels EU Quarter
item.description: A young person was injured on Monday afternoon following an attack with a bladed weapon in the European quarter in Brussels.

item.title: Police spread images of suspects arson Anderlecht
item.description: Police have spread images of three suspects in a case of arson in the Rue Hoorickx in Anderlecht on 1 August 2026.

item.title: Brussels City Council remains undecided on Grand Casino concession
item.description: The Brussels City Council has not yet decided on the new concession holder for the Grand Casino.

item.title: One in two cigarettes smoked in Belgium is either foreign or counterfeit
item.description: More than half of cigarette packets collected in Belgium now come from abroad or are counterfeit, with the proportion rising sharply over the past year.

item.title: Brussels takes back its streets on Car-Free Sunday: 'It is a bit like a Utopia'
item.description: Cars out, people in. For nine and a half hours on Sunday, Brussels belonged to people on foot, bikes and skateboards.

item.title: 'Very serious': Two Brussels art schools file complaint against teacher who allegedly violated students
item.description: Two Brussels art schools have referred allegations of sexual violence against a former teacher to prosecutors after several female students came forward.

item.title: Healthcare providers call for parliamentary inquiry into Belgium's health insurance funds
item.description: Belgian healthcare providers are calling for parliamentary scrutiny of the country's health insurance funds amid concerns over their governance, financial flows and potential conflicts of interest.

item.title: Belgian Alzheimer's carers spend up to 139 hours a week caring for loved ones
item.description: Family carers of people with Alzheimer's provide up to 139 hours of care a week, taking a considerable toll on their work, wellbeing and finances.

item.title: Firefighters evacuate 60 residents from apartment building on fire in Anderlecht
item.description: The seat of the fire was quickly identified near the rubbish storage area and was soon brought under control.

item.title: Eight comic artists honored with Atomium Awards at Brussels comic festival
item.description: Nearly €85,000 in prize money and support was awarded during opening.

item.title: Hundreds of people gather for 'Belgium's longest lunch table' at Meise Botanic Garden
item.description: It is an attempt to break the record for Belgium’s longest lunch table and draw attention to child poverty.

item.title: Fire scorches multi-studio apartment building in Ixelles
item.description: The fire started at about 11:45 in a studio on the third floor of the four-storey building.

item.title: One person seriously injured in stabbing in Anderlecht overnight
item.description: Initial findings suggest the victim was attacked in the street by one person. The motive for the assault is not yet known.

item.title: Weekend heritage days in Brussels see over 270 events in their program
item.description: The weekend programme includes guided tours, walks, cycle rides, exhibitions, lectures, performances and special openings.

item.title: More than 270 ways to discover Brussels differently this weekend with Heritage Days
item.description: The 38th edition of the Heritage Days takes place on Saturday 19 and Sunday 20 September, with more than 270 activities across the capital’s 19 municipalities.

item.title: Brussels goes car-free on Sunday: Everything you need to know
item.description: Brussels will go car-free on Sunday, with free public transport, activities across the capital and special events marking 50 years of the Brussels Metro. Here's everything you need to know.

item.title: Brussels taxi industry protests 'Ten years of being stifled by multinationals'
item.description: Protesters say that a decade of political inaction and competition from multinationals such as Uber is squeezing their livelihoods.

item.title: Crackdown on LGBTQ+ people in Turkey has troubling link to Brussels
item.description: A fierce crackdown on LGBTQ+ people in Turkey has led to raids and arrests, and the fallout is now even reaching Brussels, where people will take to the streets in protest.

item.title: King Baudouin Foundation invests over €1 million for cycling infrastructure projects in Brussels
item.description: For this second edition, an independent jury selected six projects completed in 2024 or 2025.
